notes.title: Operating frequency
notes.body:
Data is 5 bytes (10-byte BCD), little-endian. Digit order: byte-1 low = 10 Hz, byte-1 high = 1 Hz, byte-2 low = 1 kHz, byte-2 high = 100 Hz, byte-3 low = 100 kHz, byte-3 high = 10 kHz, byte-4 low = 10 MHz, byte-4 high = 1 MHz, byte-5 low = 1 GHz (0-1), byte-5 high = 100 MHz (0-4 on IC-9700).
Example: 144.000000 MHz -> 00 00 00 44 01

Commands 00 / 03 / 05 read or set transceive frequency; command 1C 03 reads the transmit frequency in Split.

notes.title: Operating mode
notes.body:
Data is 1-2 bytes.
Byte 1 - operating mode: 00=LSB, 01=USB, 02=AM, 03=CW, 04=RTTY, 05=FM, 07=CW-R, 08=RTTY-R, 17=DV, 22=DD (DD selectable only when 1200 MHz band is set to other than satellite mode).
Byte 2 - filter: 01=FIL1, 02=FIL2, 03=FIL3 (optional with commands 01 and 06; FIL1/default selected when omitted).

notes.title: Band edge frequency settings
notes.body:
Band edge frequencies are sent as pairs of BCD-encoded frequencies, one pair per edge:
  byte 1: edge number (01-1E = 1-30) (not returned when reading by command 02)
  bytes 2-6: lower edge frequency (5-byte BCD, same encoding as command 05)
  byte 7: separator 2D (fixed)
  bytes 8-12: higher edge frequency (5-byte BCD)

Command 02 reads band edges for the selected band (1.2 GHz uses 3-byte frequency encoding); commands 1E 01 / 1E 03 read or set numbered band edges.

notes.title: Scope waveform data
notes.body:
Outputs the waveform data to the controller.
q Main or Sub scope data
• 00=Main scope, 01=Sub scope
w Order of division data (Current): 01~11
e Division number (Maximum): 01(LAN), 11(USB)
When data is sent to the controller through the
LAN port, all data is sent together. However,
when the data is sent through the USB port, the
data is divided by 11 and sent in sequential order.
The 1st data sends only the wave information (q ~
y) without the waveform data (u).
The 2nd or later data sends the minimum wave
information (q ~ e) with waveform data (u).
r Center or Fixed mode data
• 00 = Center mode scope,
01 = Fixed mode scope
t Waveform information
The waveform information is different between
the Center mode and the Fixed mode.
• In the Center mode:  Center frequency and span are
sent
See page 13 for Operating frequency data, and the
Scope span settings to the right.
• In the Fixed mode:  Lower edge and higher edge
frequencies are sent
See page 25 for Scope Fixed edge frequency
settings e ~ !2.
y Out of range information
• 00 = In range, 01 = Out of range
If the scope data is out of range, the waveform data
(u) is omitted.
u Waveform data
The transceiver outputs the drawn waveform data.
The data range or data length of the waveform data is
judged by the controller. (The data range is basically
the same as the display size of the scope on the
controller.)
Data range 0 ~ 160
Data length 475
